problem:
Find, **in ascending order and rounded to one decimal place**, the two solutions to the equation $\operatorname{sec}⁡x=\frac{4}{3}$ for $0\le x<2\pi .$

**In ascending order,** the solutions are $x=$
{{field-1}}
and $x=$ 
{{field-2}}.
worked_solution:
Recall that $\operatorname{sec}⁡x=\frac{1}{\operatorname{cos}⁡x}.$ Therefore the given equation is equivalent to

$$
\operatorname{cos}⁡x=\frac{3}{4}.
$$

First, we find the principal value of $x,$ rounded to three decimal places:

$$
{x}_{1}=arccos\,(\frac{3}{4})≈0.723
$$

Our first solution lies in the $1$st quadrant and has a reference angle of ${\theta }_{R}≈0.723.$ Since $\operatorname{cos}⁡x>0,$ the second solution must lie in the $4$th quadrant, and it also has a reference angle ${\theta }_{R}≈0.723.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13977622/assets/3b95f4a3d92d2214472f8c72f9322f6d1aa89a6e2c4f8cc2ae9f13015217a84d.png)

Since the second solution ${x}_{2}$ lies in the $4$th quadrant, we can find it using the reference angle as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{2} & =2\pi -{\theta }_{R} \\  & ≈2\pi -0.723 \\  & ≈5.560\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, in ascending order and rounded to one decimal place, the solutions are $x=0.7$ and $x=5.6.$
